blockers.issue: Citation provenance is still not enforced on the final persisted citation set. validateForEmit checks only payload.citations, but canonicalize later calls normalizeCitations(next.citations, next.sources), so an emitted payload can pass with one grounded citation and still persist arbitrary ungrounded URLs supplied in sources/link/href-style entries. This bypasses the B3 guarantee that every saved citation URL came from fetchedUrls or searchResultUrls.

fetchedUrls is populated by extractUrlsFromToolResult(event.result), which recursively scans the entire fetch_page result including the untrusted page markdown. A URL merely mentioned or linked inside a fetched page is therefore treated as if it was itself fetched, so a malicious/low-quality page can smuggle arbitrary citation URLs through the provenance gate. fetchedUrls should be derived from the actual fetch_page request/result URL, not every URL in third-party content.

The loadPending shared-promise race is fixed, but pending reverse persistence is still not serialized. Multiple concurrent writes can mutate pendingReverses and set pendingDirty while another write is between atomicWriteJson and pendingDirty=false; the earlier flush can then clear the dirty flag for a later mutation that was not included in its serialized file, losing pending reverse updates on disk. B6 is therefore only partially addressed.

Disambiguators are wired into makeSlug and current-node canonicalization, but edge frontier keys still use makeSlug(e.type, e.name) and enqueue AgentInput without a disambiguator. Two distinct same-name edge targets are de-duplicated in FrontierQueue before either agent run can emit a disambiguator, so the original B1 same-name collision class remains for graph-expanded nodes.

warnings.issue: normalizeForProvenance drops common tracking parameters but does not sort query parameters or handle tracking keys case-insensitively, so equivalent URLs with reordered query strings or uppercase UTM parameters can fail to match. This is a false-negative risk rather than a grounding bypass.

AgentDeps.maxEmitAttempts still has a stale comment saying the Nth attempt accepts best-effort payloads. The emit_node tool description and runtime implementation are now strict, but this public interface comment can mislead future maintainers.

The claimed/inFlight budget invariant appears correct in code, but the comment still says the crawler may exceed maxNodes by concurrency - 1 writes. With the current pre-run reservation check it should not exceed maxNodes; the stale comment makes this harder to audit.

summary: FAIL: Round-3 fixes addressed many previous findings: separate search/fetch counters are present, untrusted_page and untrusted_search_results wrappers were added, schema edge target types and disk floors are stronger, the fallback emit escape hatch is removed, lock cleanup and webhook validation were improved, assert-cache now requires 100% citation coverage, Firecrawl /v2/search fallback exists, and typecheck plus the non-live test suite pass. Blockers remain around citation provenance after canonicalization, over-broad URL extraction from fetched page content, unsynchronized pending-reverse flushing, and frontier de-duplication that still drops same-name edge targets before disambiguation.
